messages:
sam: heads-up — HF model bring-up failing conv-qa-small evals after jinja->redwood conversion, looks like sentinel tokens are leaking into user messages :thinking_face:

tara: can you paste a minimal before/after render?

sam: sure, minimal example — original template:
```jinja
{% for m in messages %}
{{ m.role }}: {{ m.content }}\n{% endfor %}
```
After conversion (what RW gets):
```text
user: hi
[SYS] <|assistant|> system: you are a helpful assistant
assistant: hello
```
Note the `[SYS] <|assistant|>` fragment ended up inline inside the user turn.

miguel: my guess is config.json "additional_special_tokens" mismatch + the jinja prerender step collapsing newline boundaries. HF chat_template sometimes stores system as a pseudo-message token; our converter is naively joining blocks without role separators.

ellie: quick numbers from local quant-8 test: baseline float eval EM=74.2, after conversion+quant EM=68.1 and sometimes hallucinated system prompts in outputs.

ci-bot: quick-infra-check: job redwood-ci/model-bringup #112 failed on unit-tests -> converter_test::role_boundary_check

sam: repro command: `python infra/tools/convert_chattemplate.py --model ./hf-mirror/model-x --out redwood-format`
When I inspect the converted prompt bytes there's an invisible U+FFF0 sentinel between lines, e.g. "user: hi\uFFF0system: ..." so tokenizer sees the system token as part of user text.

tara: probable fix: ensure converter inserts explicit role delimiter token (we use `<|role_sep|>`) between rendered blocks, and treat `additional_special_tokens` from config.json as single tokens when tokenizing. Also avoid collapsing trailing newlines in Jinja by rendering with `keep_trailing_newline=True` or similar.

miguel: another thing — KV cache padding in runtime expects role boundaries aligned to tok indices. If a sentinel gets glued to the user token, continuous-batching will shift KV offsets by 1 and cause cache drift for subsequent tokens (seen in long chat evals). We should add a non-embedded boundary token (a no-op sentinel) or reserve index 0 for role_sep to avoid embedding lookup shifts.

ellie: can we run a canary on the private cluster? would like to see quant+kvcache effect end-to-end before pushing PR.

sam: yes, I'll patch converter to add explicit `<|role_sep|>` and update tokenizer config merging; will run canary on private-dedicated pool. will post results. :thumbsup:

tara: I'll open PR with tests (unit: role_boundary_check, integration: conv-qa-small regression) and link to ticket INC-4321. tagging @miguel to review KV cache notes. :eyes:

miguel: ack, will review and add a short fuzz test for invisible unicode sentinels.

ellie: thanks — if we can keep the sentinel out of user tokens the quant regressions should drop. good luck.
